stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and null spec. Live Preview is a complex feature involving real-time content rendering across GO, UP, and MX variants. Openspec needed first to elaborate requirements and define ACs; speckit then hardens with testability, edge cases, and security checks (e.g., auth for preview endpoints, XSS in preview rendering, concurrent edit conflicts).

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a new Live Preview capability for Contentstack CMS editing. No existing code implements preview mode. The primary attachment point is useContent (236 callers), the single chokepoint for all content delivery. All Contentstack* components consume content through it and would inherit preview behavior automatically. ACs are empty; VCs are derived from the description alone.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria, so this entire list is built from the story title, description, and technical context. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/2/3 cover the core Live Preview protocol — parameter detection, real-time updates, and entry switching. (2) AC-4/5 ensure the preview state is visually and accessibly communicated. (3) AC-6 is the regression safeguard ensuring non-preview mode is untouched. (4) AC-7/8 cover error and edge cases (connection loss, missing entries). (5) AC-9/13/14 are security criteria — preventing draft content leakage to production users, ensuring URL sharing doesn't expose unpublished content, and ensuring session-bound preview access. (6) AC-10 addresses the publish-during-preview edge case. (7) AC-11 covers reference field resolution in preview — a common Contentstack Live Preview pitfall. (8) AC-12 ensures cross-site consistency per the [GO, UP, MX] scope. (9) AC-15 specifically calls out ContentstackLink since it was listed as a key file and is a content-consuming component that must participate in preview. CAVEAT: Without reading the actual file contents, the criteria reference 'query parameters' as the most common Contentstack Live Preview trigger, but the actual mechanism could differ based on the SDK version and configuration in useContent.ts.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Pipeline broke: openspec was assigned to elaborate requirements and define ACs for a story with empty acceptance criteria, but its contribution is limited to technical context notes (useContent chokepoint, 236 callers, Contentstack* consumers) with acceptanceChanged=false and splitCount=0. Openspec did not produce any acceptance criteria. Speckit then compensated by building all 15 ACs from the title/description alone, effectively performing both elaboration and hardening roles. While speckit's output is thorough (security criteria, edge cases, cross-site scope, reference field resolution, ContentstackLink participation), it was built without openspec's intended technical depth and speckit itself flagged a caveat that actual file contents were not read, meaning query-parameter assumptions about the Live Preview trigger mechanism are unverified. Both agents did add value — openspec provided useful architectural context, speckit provided comprehensive AC coverage — but the value was not non-overlapping in the intended sense; speckit had to do openspec's job. Human review needed to validate the 15 generated ACs against actual codebase behavior and Contentstack SDK configuration.
